guides-essential-tools.s81: The siphon (Gravel Vacuum) pulls debris from between the gravel without removing the gravel. This prevents the buildup of organic material that anaerobic bacteria convert into hydrogen sulfide — the toxic, foul odor. The mesh is essential for transport or isolation — not for chasing.

guides-essential-tools.s102: Does everything eat the same food? No.
guides-essential-tools.s103: Shrimp are divided into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores. Wrong food — even if the shrimp eat it — leads to long‑term nutritional deficiencies. Overfeeding is more dangerous than underfeeding — it quickly pollutes the water and raises ammonia.

guides-essential-tools.s114: Important — its core is in the filter
guides-essential-tools.s116: Biological media are sponge, ceramic, or plastic materials inside the filter. Their large surface area allows beneficial bacteria to grow and multiply.
guides-essential-tools.s117: The biofilm (bacterial layer) grows on these surfaces — do not clean it with tap water. Clean it only with the tank water in a separate container.
guides-essential-tools.s118: Media types: sponge (can be cleaned), ceramic rings (Ceramic Rings — long‑lasting), Bioball (for larger filters). Quantity and quality matter more than type.

guides-water-myths.s74: Products such as chlorine removers, pH regulators, and ammonia products each have a specific function and specific conditions. Using them without understanding the cause can muddle the water chemistry or mask a problem instead of solving it.
guides-water-myths.s75: Example: Some "detoxifier" products temporarily convert ammonia into a less toxic form — the test shows zero but it is still present. The substrate looks fine on the surface — the problem hasn't been resolved.

guides-decor-stones.s46: Aquarium Decor & Stones — What’s Safe and What Alters Water
guides-decor-stones.s47: The safe stones for an aquarium are inert stones that do not alter water chemistry: basalt, quartz, travertine, and polished river stones. Avoid marble and limestone as they raise pH. Wash all decor in clean water without soap before placing it in the tank. Aquarium wood is safe but may tint water yellow from tannins — this is normal. guides-water-test-guide.s74: Ammonia is produced from: fish waste, leftover food, dead plants, and any organic material that degrades in water. Beneficial bacteria in the filter convert it to nitrite and then nitrate — this is the biological cycle.

guides-tank-rescue-plan.s60: If the plan fails — what do you do?
guides-tank-rescue-plan.s61: You followed the steps in sequence, reached Day 30, and the fish has not improved noticeably — this is not a failure. It means there is an unidentified variable.
guides-tank-rescue-plan.s63: Ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, pH. Sometimes the issue lies in pH or accumulated nitrates — not just ammonia. A single test on Day 0 is insufficient.
guides-tank-rescue-plan.s65: The filter appears to be running, but flow may be weak or the biological media damaged. Clean only the mechanical media — do not touch the biological media yet.
guides-tank-rescue-plan.s66: Refer to the treatment guide if the fish shows symptoms

guides-tank-rescue-plan.s70: If the fish continues to die — send a photo to AQUAVO
guides-tank-rescue-plan.s71: Rapid mortality (more than one fish per day) indicates either acute poisoning or an infectious disease. Send a photo of the tank and test results — diagnosis from a clear image is faster and more accurate than any other step.
guides-tank-rescue-plan.s72: Do not start a second rescue plan before you know why the first failed. Every random step adds pressure to the tank — it’s not a solution.
